9669               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9670               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9671               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9672               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9673               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9674               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9675               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9676               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9677               	; 	'
9678               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9679               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9680               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9681               	; 	'
9682               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9683               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9684               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9685               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9686               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9687               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9688               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9689               	; 	'
9690               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9691               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9692               	; 	'
9693               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9694               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9695               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9696               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9697               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9698               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9699               	; 	'

9703               	; 	' before any of this.
9704               	; 	'
9705               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9706               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9707               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the

10151               	;
10152               	; 	' ======================================================================
10153               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10154               	; 	' ======================================================================
10155               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10156               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10157               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10158               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10159               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10160               	; 	'
10161               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10162               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10163               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10164               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10165               	; 	' broken.
10166               	; 	'
10167               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10168               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10169               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10170               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10171               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10172               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10173               	; 	'
10174               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10175               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10176               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10177               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10178               	; coll_obst:
10179               cvb_COLL_OBST
10180               	; 	IF klst = ST_ESC THEN RETURN		' riding is invincible, per the
10181 DEF2 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLST,r0
     DEF4 21BC

     DEF8 0300

10477               	; 	' ONE PASS LONGER THAN THE SOUND, because the sound does not start here.
10478               	; 	' sfh is a latch that sfx_tick consumes on the NEXT pass, so the note
10479               	; 	' runs passes 2..HITSND+1 of the freeze and this ends with it.
10480               	; 	hfz = HITSND + 1
10481 E172 0200  20 	li r0,5376   ; 21*256
     E174 1500     
10482 E176 D800  38 	movb r0,@cvb_HFZ
     E178 2198     
10483               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10484               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10485               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10486               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10487               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10488               	; 	' away from.
10489               	; 	'
10490               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10491               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10492               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10493               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10494               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10495               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10496               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10497               	; 	'
10498               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10499               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10500               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10501               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10502               	; 	'
10503               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10504               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10505               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10506               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10507               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10508               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10509               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10510               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10511               	; 	'
10512               	; 	' A ducking Kop is still stood up, because the crouch is a held pose and
10513               	; 	' there is nothing to interrupt.
10514               	; 	IF klst <> ST_JUMP THEN

10717               	; 	' RIDING WITH THE DOORS SHUT: HIDE HIM AND DO NOT DRAW HIM AT ALL.
10718               	; 	'
10719               	; 	' This test used to sit AFTER his sprites had been written, so every pass
10720               	; 	' placed him at his old floor and then hid him again. That is not free.
10721               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
10722               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
10723               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
10724               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
10725               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
10726               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.
10727               	; 	'

11849               	; 	' ======================================================================
11850               	; 	' THE SCANNER
11851               	; 	' ======================================================================
11852               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
11853               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
11854               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
11855               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
11856               	; 	'
11857               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
11858               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
11859               	; 	'
11860               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
11861               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
11862               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
11863               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
11864               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
11865               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
11866               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
11867               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
11868               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
11869               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
11870               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
11871               	; esc_tick:
11872               cvb_ESC_TICK
11873               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
11874               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
11875               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
11876               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).

11896               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
11897               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
11898               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
11899               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
11900               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
11901               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
11902               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
11903               	; 	'
11904               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
11905               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
11906               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
11907               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
11908               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
11909               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
11910               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.
11911               	; 	escp = escp + 1

11923               cv810
11924               	; 	' ONLY THE CELLS THAT MOVE, AND ONLY THIS SCREEN'S. genart.py measures
11925               	; 	' which cells move -- the step cells and the COMPOSITE copies of them
11926               	; 	' that cross a floor -- and groups them WEST then EAST, because only one
11927               	; 	' direction is ever on screen: screen 0 carries a west flight and screen
11928               	; 	' 7 an east one.
11929               	; 	'
11930               	; 	' THIS IS THE ONLY PER-PASS WORK UNIQUE TO THESE TWO SCREENS, and it is
11931               	; 	' `define_char`, which in bitmap mode is LDIRVM3 -- the TRIPLE copy, once
11932               	; 	' per screen third. It therefore costs three times what the character
11933               	; 	' count suggests, which is why these screens run slower than the rest.
11934               	; 	'
11935               	; 	' THE WEST SCREEN USED TO COST HALF AS MUCH AGAIN, because it carries TWO
11936               	; 	' flights: floor 1's crosses into a shop floor and floor 3's into the
11937               	; 	' roof, so it needed both composite sets -- nine characters against the
11938               	; 	' east's six, 216 bytes a pass against 144. It measured 20 passes a
11939               	; 	' second where the east screen managed 24-26. The two sets are
11940               	; 	' PIXEL-IDENTICAL and are never wanted in the same screen THIRD, so they
11941               	; 	' share their characters now and are told apart by the per-third colour
11942               	; 	' table (see esc_deck_col in setup). Six either side.
11943               	; 	'

12207               	;
12208               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12209               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12210               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12211               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12212               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12213               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12214               	; 	'
12215               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12216               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12217               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12218               	; 	'
12219               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12220               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12221               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12222               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12223               	; 	'
12224               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12225               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12226               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12227               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12228               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12229               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12230               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12231               	; 	'
12232               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12233               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12234               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12235               	; 	'
12236               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12237               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12238               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.

12580               	;
12581               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
12582               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12583               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12584               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12585               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12586               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12587               	; scan_wipe:
12588               cvb_SCAN_WIPE
12589               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12590               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12591               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12592               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12593               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12594               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12595               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12596               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12597               	; 	'
12598               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12599               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12600               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12601               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12602               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12603               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12604               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12605               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12606               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12607               	; 	'
12608               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12609               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12610               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
12611               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
12612               	; 	'
12613               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and
12614               	; 	' checkstruct.py fails the build if the two disagree.

13625               	;
13626               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
13627               	; 	'
13628               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
13629               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
13630               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
13631               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
13632               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
13633               	; 	'
13634               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
13635               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
13636               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
13637               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
13638               	; 	' counting stops.
13639               	;
13640               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
13641               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
13642               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
13643               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
13644               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
13645               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
13646               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
13647               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
13648               	; 	'
13649               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
13650               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
13651               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

13806               	;
13807               	; 	' Silence every channel FIRST. SOUND latches, and the per-channel decay
13808               	; 	' counters are not ticked inside this loop -- a tone still sounding when
13809               	; 	' the pause starts would hang for its whole duration, which is the classic
13810               	; 	' CVBasic sticky-audio failure.
13811               	; 	' EVERY CHANNEL OFF, AND THE DECAY COUNTERS WITH THEM. The counters are
13812               	; 	' ticked by the main loop, so anything still sounding when the loop stops
13813               	; 	' -- for a capture, a death, the bonus count -- sustains for as long as
13814               	; 	' whatever replaced the loop takes. That is where the long beep over the
13815               	; 	' bonus tally came from: not the tally's own note, which turns itself off
13816               	; 	' after every unit, but a footstep or a hit that was still ringing when
13817               	; 	' Harry was caught.
13818               	; snd_off:
13819               cvb_SND_OFF
13820               	; 	' EVERY CHANNEL sfx_tick CAN WRITE, AND CHANNEL 3 IS ONE OF THEM. This
13821               	; 	' routine was written when the footstep was a pair of tones on channel 0
13822               	; 	' and it still named only 0, 1 and 2 after the footstep moved to the
13823               	; 	' NOISE channel. So a step ringing when Harry was caught was never turned
13824               	; 	' off: it hissed through the whole bonus tally and did not stop until the
13825               	; 	' next round's first footstep happened to reset it.
13826               	; 	'
13827               	; 	' Zeroing sot does NOT silence it. The counter only emits its note-off on
13828               	; 	' the pass it reaches zero, so setting it to zero by hand skips the very

14254               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14255               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14256               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14257               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14258               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14259               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14260               	;
14261               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14262               	; 	'
14263               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14264               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14265               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14266               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14267               	; 	'
14268               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14269               	; 	'
14270               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14271               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14272               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14273               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14274               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14275               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14276               	; 	'
14277               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14278               	; 	'
14279               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14280               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14281               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14282               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14283               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14284               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14285               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14286               	; 	'
14287               	; 	' 104 px/s over 15 px is 6.9 a second -- between the 8.0 that read as
14288               	; 	' slightly hurried and the 6.1 that read as trudging. The dial is this one
14289               	; 	' constant and the subtraction below, which must stay threshold + 1 or the
14290               	; 	' carry is wrong.
14291               	; 	'
14292               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14293               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14294               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14295               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14296               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14297               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14298               	; 	'
14299               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14300               	; 	'
14301               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14302               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14303               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14304               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14305               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14306               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not

14431               	;
14432               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14433               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14434               	; 	'
14435               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14436               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14437               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14438               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14439               	; 	'
14440               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14441               	; 	'
14442               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14443               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14444               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14445               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14446               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14447               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14448               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14449               	; 	'
14450               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14451               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14452               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14453               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14454               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14455               	; 	'
14456               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14457               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14458               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14459               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14460               	; 	#if TI994A
14461               	; 	BANK 2
14462      02CC     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

14600               	;
14601               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($14 = black ink on dark blue).
14602               	; 	'
14603               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
14604               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
14605               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
14606               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
14607               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
14608               	; 	'
14609               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
14610               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
14611               	;

14613               cvb_FONT_COL

15126               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15127               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15128               	; 	'
15129               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15130               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15131               	; 	' being small sprites.
15132               	; 	'
15133               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15134               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15135               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15136               	; 	'
15137               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15138               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15139               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15140               	;
15141               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60

16399               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16400               	; 	'
16401               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16402               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16403               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16404               	; 	'
16405               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16406               	; 	' blit is
16407               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16408               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16409               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16410               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16411               	; 	'
16412               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16413               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16414               	; 	'
16415               	; 	' template ids:
16416               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16417               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16418               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16419               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16420               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16421               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16422               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16423               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16424               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16425               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16426               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16427               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16428               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16429               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
